subject.title: fix: active-memory recall fails with billing rejections on subscription-only Claude CLI setups

question: Should restricted embedded helper runs enter CLI subprocesses through a generic backend capability, or may active-memory keep the proposed Claude-specific core dispatch and loopback-MCP grant seam?
rationale: The patch changes auth selection, process execution, and tool-capability minting across core runtime and gateway boundaries; code review cannot choose the permanent ownership and trust model without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt a backend capability
options.body: Move the dispatch decision to CLI backend/runtime capability metadata and let active-memory request the generic restricted-helper behavior.

options.title: Approve the current seam
options.body: Explicitly accept the Claude-specific core dispatch mode and per-run MCP grant as the supported permanent contract.

options.title: Pause for broader dispatch work
options.body: Keep the targeted issue open and fold the implementation into the canonical helper-runtime work tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/57326.

recommendation.title: Adopt a backend capability
recommendation.body: Move the dispatch decision to CLI backend/runtime capability metadata and let active-memory request the generic restricted-helper behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most directly connects this owner candidate to Claude CLI runtime and session behavior, while active-memory owners can review the caller-side deadline contract.
